title: Depth-first search
summary: Go as deep as you can along one path, and back up only when you hit a dead end. Recursion does the backing up.

checkpoints.text: DFS starts at 0 and marks it visited.
From 0 it went to 1, then from 1 to 3, then from 3 to 2: always the first unvisited neighbour, deeper and deeper. Look at the call stack: one frame per vertex on the current path.
From 2 it went on to 4, then 5. Vertex 5's neighbours are all visited: a dead end.

The calls return one by one, each checking whether its vertex has any unvisited neighbours left. None do, so DFS is finished: 0 1 3 2 4 5. A stack (here, the call stack) is what makes it go deep first, where BFS's queue made it go wide.
